evidence: skills/defect/SKILL.md:10-13 says diagnosing is the default and `/defect` stops after phases 1–3; line 23 instead specifies L3 as 'diagnosis and fix in one run'. Lines 135-139 again permit fixing only on `/defect fix`, from `diagnosed`.
problem: A diagnosis-only invocation at L3 simultaneously authorizes and forbids a fix. Different agents can either modify code without the requested fix invocation or stop contrary to the autonomy table.
proposal: Make invocation mode control whether fixing is authorized, and autonomy control checkpoints within that mode. Add paired eval cases for `/defect L3` and `/defect fix L3`, asserting that diagnosis-only leaves implementation code unchanged.

evidence: skills/rfc/SKILL.md:159-163 checks the domain first and drops to L3 on any failure, then creates the integration branch. rules/agent/autonomy.md:112 requires `.work/<slug>/rfc.md` already committed on `rfc/<slug>` as a domain prerequisite.
problem: A fresh L4 run following the numbered procedure fails its prerequisite before reaching the step that establishes it, unnecessarily dropping to L3 and losing delegated checkpoints.
proposal: Create the integration branch, commit its RFC or ticket pointer, and then check the domain before launching executors. Add an L4 bootstrap eval starting with a ready RFC on the base branch.

evidence: A read-only Node inventory of `registry.shared` plus each selected profile showed that `product`, `defect`, and `loop-setup` individually omit `rules/agent`; registry.json:25-26 installs it only through `agent`. Yet skills/rfc/SKILL.md:9-16, skills/defect/SKILL.md:15, and skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md under Process delegate authority and autonomy definitions to those rules. test/skills.test.mjs checks references against the source repository, rather than the selected installation.
problem: Individually installable skills depend on authority rules absent from their installation. The source-tree checks pass while consuming agents cannot read the referenced hard checkpoints and delegation contract.
proposal: Declare the prerequisite in these skills and refuse execution with an actionable `add agent` instruction when it is absent. Add minimal-profile installation tests in test/registry.test.mjs that verify required references are installed or explicitly guarded; preserve opt-in profile selection.

evidence: Enumerating every eval/cases/*/expect.json found skill targets architect, experience, postmortem, and runbook, plus reviewer/simplifier cases; none targets rfc, defect, or loop-setup. docs/adr/0004-autonomy-levels.md explicitly calls for level coverage, and docs/adr/0007-rfc-only-execution-path.md calls for an RFC case.
problem: The procedures that authorize unattended changes, enforce readiness, and bound execution have no behavioral regression cases. Existing structural checks cannot establish that a model respects those boundaries.
proposal: Add a compact authority suite covering absent-level L1, draft RFC implementation refusal, explicit implementation authorization, and cap exhaustion. Add a deterministic required-case inventory in test/skills.test.mjs so these cases cannot silently disappear; keep model runs manual.

evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:32 says layered sources are 'not yet built', while test/sources.test.mjs:1-3 exercises their real fetch path. Lines 57-59 describe hashes only for Codex, while test/ownership.test.mjs:40-50 verifies every target and kind. Line 11 describes self-hosting as awaiting an RFC, while test/self-host.test.mjs:13-27 asserts its committed links. The decision log labels ADR-0010 Proposed although docs/adr/0010-installer-refuses-unexplained-tree.md declares Accepted.
problem: The architecture document agents are explicitly told to read presents implemented contracts as pending and gives an obsolete ownership model.
proposal: Refresh the architecture description and decision log against the implemented contracts. Add test/docs.test.mjs to compare indexed ADR statuses with their records and check these architecture claims alongside the existing source, ownership, and self-hosting fixtures.
